from pypdf import PdfReader
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
seen=set()
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):

from pathlib import Path
import re,statistics
text=Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').read_text()
for page,heading,n in [(9,'MMLU-Bangla',3),(9,'MMLU-Marathi',3),(10,'MMLU-Hindi',6),(10,'Belebele-Tamil',4),(11,'Belebele-Telugu',4)]:
 p=text.split(f'===== PAGE {page} =====')[1].split('===== PAGE')[0]
 block=p.split(heading,1)[1].split('Table',1)[0]
 for line in block.splitlines()[1:]:
  fields=re.split(r'\\s{2,}',line.strip())
  if len(fields)<n+2: continue
  try:
   vals=[float(x) for x in fields[1:]]
  except ValueError: continue
  calc=statistics.mean(vals[:n]); reported=vals[n]
  if abs(calc-reported)>.02:
   print(f'Page {page}, {fields[0]}: reported mean {reported:.2f}, recalculated {calc:.2f}; component scores {vals[:n]}')

strengths: The paper addresses a clear NLP need: accessible generative models for ten Indian languages, including underserved languages such as Konkani, Maithili, Odia, and Sanskrit. The small parameter sizes make CPU deployment a relevant practical objective.

The work describes substantial model-building and data-curation effort, including monolingual, bilingual, and multilingual models, culturally grounded prompts, and manually authored Bangla instructions.

The evaluation includes established benchmarks alongside human judgments. Some reported instruction-tuning gains are promising: Hindi Belebele accuracy increases from 23.33 to 42.78, and Bangla Belebele from 25.11 to 32.45. These warrant further validation.
weaknesses: The central RoPE memory-saving claim is unsupported. Rescaling positional indices alone does not reduce the sequence-length-dependent storage of attention and activations. The paper provides neither a sufficiently specified mechanism nor controlled measurements of peak memory, throughput, and quality at different context lengths. Comparing these small models trained on one GPU with LLaMA trained on thousands of GPUs does not validate the proposed mechanism.

Reproducibility is substantially inadequate. Architecture dimensions, optimization settings, training schedules, tokenizer vocabulary sizes, precise corpus sources, unique data volumes, and multilingual sampling proportions are missing. The manuscript supplies no access link or availability statement for its models, tokenizers, code, or datasets. The reported 95/5 split and generic deduplication description also do not establish document-level separation or benchmark decontamination.

The benchmark results do not establish the claimed low-resource-to-high-resource transfer or avoidance of the curse of multilinguality. For example, mParamanu obtains 24.84 on Hindi MMLU and 25.44 on Hindi Belebele, both approximately the 25% chance level. Small differences around chance require uncertainty estimates and appropriate controls. Attributing improvements to script grouping, typology, or comparable corpora requires ablations controlling model capacity, training data, and compute.

The human evaluation is too limited to support broad superiority claims: only four prompts per language and three generations per prompt are described. Annotator allocation, blinding, the selection rule for 'top-3,' agreement, and uncertainty are unreported. Factuality scoring conflates unverifiable content with false content. Literary prompts also require checks against memorization of training books. Several generation baselines are primarily English-focused, while the GPT-3.5 comparison relies on a 2023 web interface without a reproducible, matched generation protocol.

The tokenizer contribution is underspecified and insufficiently validated. Figure 3 does not explain how BPE and Unigram models, vocabularies, or segmentation decisions are combined. Figure 2 does not establish that fertility was measured on identical held-out text under comparable conditions. Moreover, Section 4.5.1 interprets perplexities across different languages and tokenizers as directly comparable; these values have different prediction units and data distributions. The tokenizer comparison needs controlled downstream evaluation and a common normalization for likelihood.

The practical efficiency evidence is incomplete. Table 18 reports CPU tokens per second without identifying the processor, thread count, runtime, batch size, or input/output lengths, and provides no baseline measurements. Different tokenizers also make tokens per second an incomplete comparison of useful text throughput. These omissions prevent verification of the deployment claims and attribution of efficiency to the proposed methods.

Internal inconsistencies undermine result traceability. In Table 7, the six Hindi instruction-tuned scores average 38.49, not the reported 40.14. The instruction dataset is described as 23,000 examples, but Section 4.5.2 refers to 27,000 and, for Hindi, an additional 52,000 Alpaca examples. Table 12 alternates between three and five generations. Together with the unsupported central claims and missing implementation details, these issues require substantial methodological documentation and new controlled evaluations before a sound Findings recommendation is possible.
